title: $22 an Hour vs a $48k Salary: Who Earns More?

scenes.say: Jade's $48,000 salary really paid about $18 an hour.
She had two offers: $22 an hour, or $48,000 a year. The salary sounded bigger.
But the salary job expected about 50 hours a week, with no overtime.
The hourly job: 40 hours at $22, plus about 4 hours of overtime at $33.
That's roughly $52,600 a year, working 6 fewer hours every week.
Benefits matter too, so she compared the whole offer, not one number.
Divide by your real hours, and the bigger number isn't always bigger.
What's your real hourly pay? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because a $48k salary can mean $18 an hour.

question: Divide your pay by the hours you really work: what's your real hourly rate?
description: Jade compared $22 an hour with a $48,000 salary. The salary job expected about 50 hours a week with no overtime, roughly $18.46 an hour, while the hourly job with about 4 overtime hours paid around $52,600. Benefits matter too. Numbers are rounded US estimates.
